title: 49ers TE George Kittle close to practicing, has ‘a chance’ to play in opener
content:
San Francisco 49ers star tight end George Kittle said Sunday he’s nearing a return to practice from his torn Achilles tendon, and he hopes to be ready to play in the Sept. 10 season opener against the Los Angeles Rams in Australia.

Kittle said he’s “very confident” he will be activated from the physically unable to perform list before Week 1, meaning he would not miss the season’s first four games. As for facing the Rams?

“I have a chance,” Kittle said. “We’re running around a lot, hitting top speeds. Hopefully we’re back in pads practicing sooner than later. Just trying to check the boxes and not be a dumbass.”

Kittle, who turns 33 in October, tore the Achilles in his right leg on Jan. 11 in the wild-card playoffs against the Philadelphia Eagles. He said his surgeon, Dr. Neal ElAttrache, told him after the surgery he had a chance to be ready for the 2026 opener, which added motivation during his rehab.

“It was pretty easy to light a fire every day,” Kittle said.

This story will be updated.
